transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’ve been feeling… not quite here, I guess. When I’m walking across campus, it’s like I’m seeing everything through glass. Like I’m not fully in my body, and the buildings and students around me don’t feel completely real. It’s been scaring me.
When you say things don’t feel real, does this also include feeling unsure about who you are, or do you always know that you’re you?
I know I’m me. It’s more like… I’m not fully in my body, or everything around me is behind glass. The buildings, people on campus… they just feel a little unreal. That’s what scares me.
When you say things around you feel unreal, like they’re behind glass, does the world seem distorted, foggy, or far away, or does it feel like you’re in a dream?
Yeah… kind of far away, I guess. Like I’m looking at campus through glass. I’m there, but not fully in my body, and the buildings and people seem… slightly unreal. That’s the part that scares me.
Do you also feel detached from yourself, like you're observing your own thoughts or body from outside, or do you always feel connected to yourself even when the world feels unreal?

A little, yes. Not like I’m fully outside myself, but when I’m walking across campus I don’t feel completely in my body. It’s more like I’m watching things through glass, and everyone and the buildings seem… not quite real. That’s what scares me.
Does this feeling happen when you're especially anxious or having a panic attack, or does it come on even when you're feeling calm?

It’s more when I’m worked up, I think… but not only then. Sometimes I’m just walking across campus and suddenly it feels like I’m behind glass, like I’m not really in my body. The buildings and students seem a little unreal. That’s the part that scares me.
How often do you experience this feeling of being detached or as if things around you are unreal? Does it happen only occasionally, or does it come up frequently and last for long periods of time?

It comes up… more than I’d like. Not constantly, but frequent enough that I worry about it, especially walking across campus. It can feel like I’m watching everything through glass for a while—the buildings, the students—like I’m not fully in my own body.
Can you describe what happens when you feel this way? Does it feel more like you are detached from your body, or more like the world around you is detached or not real?

It’s… mostly the world, I think. Like when I’m walking across campus, everything feels like I’m seeing it through glass. The buildings and people are there, but they seem slightly unreal. And I don’t feel fully in my body either, which is what scares me.
When you feel like the world is unreal, like you’re seeing everything through glass, does this feeling go away quickly, or does it last for a long time?

It doesn’t go away right away. It can linger for a while, especially when I’m walking across campus… like I’m seeing everything through glass and I’m not quite in my body. The buildings and people feel unreal for longer than I’d like.

Have you ever felt like these experiences of unreality or detachment might be caused by something dangerous happening to you, like losing your mind or being poisoned, or do you feel like you understand that these feelings are just strange sensations that don’t make sense but aren’t based on any real danger?

I don’t really think I’m being poisoned or anything like that. It’s more… I know it doesn’t make sense, but it scares me. When I’m walking across campus and everything feels like it’s behind glass, like the buildings and students aren’t quite real and I’m not fully in my body… that’s the part that makes me worry.
Have these feelings of everything feeling unreal, like you're seeing things through glass, ever happened after a stressful or traumatic event, or do they seem to come out of nowhere?

It’s mostly when I’m walking across campus. I don’t always know what sets it off. Everything just feels… like I’m looking through glass, and I’m not fully in my body. The buildings and students seem a little unreal, and that scares me.
When you feel like you're seeing everything through glass and not fully in your body, do you also notice any gaps in your memory or find yourself in places without remembering how you got there?
I don’t think so. I mean… I haven’t found myself somewhere and not known how I got there. It’s more just that strange feeling while it’s happening.
When you feel like you're not fully in your body and everything seems unreal, do you feel more like you're detached from yourself, or more like the world around you is detached and not real?
I guess it’s both, but… mostly the world around me feels off. Like I’m walking across campus and everything is behind glass. And then I feel not quite in my body either. It’s hard to explain.

When you feel like you're not fully in your body and everything seems unreal, does this happen while your heart is racing or you're feeling short of breath, like during a panic attack, or does it happen even when your body feels calm?

It’s not always like a panic thing, I don’t think. What scares me most is walking across campus and suddenly it feels like I’m watching everything through glass… like I’m not fully in my body, and the buildings and people seem unreal.
Besides walking across campus, do you experience this feeling of unreality or detachment in other specific situations or places, such as crowded spaces, open areas, or when you're alone?

Mostly it’s the campus. I notice it when I’m walking between buildings and there are students around… everything feels kind of behind glass, like it’s not quite real. I feel a little outside myself too. I haven’t really noticed a pattern beyond that.
Do you only feel this way when you're walking across campus, or have you noticed it happening in other situations as well?

Mostly when I’m walking across campus. That’s when it hits me—the glass feeling, like I’m not quite in my body and the buildings and students don’t seem totally real. I can’t really say I’ve noticed it much elsewhere.
When you feel like you're not fully in your body and everything seems unreal, does it feel more like you're disconnected from yourself, or more like the world around you has changed and isn't real?
It’s kind of both, I guess. I feel like I’m not quite in my body, but also everything around me—buildings, students—feels sort of unreal, like I’m seeing it through glass.
When you feel this way, does it feel more like you are disconnected from yourself, as if you're not fully in your own body, or more like the world around you has changed and isn't real?

It’s… honestly both. I feel sort of outside myself, like I’m not fully in my body, and at the same time the campus around me looks unreal—like I’m watching it through glass. That’s the part that scares me.
